subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
passage:
Thursday night. The maths test was today. Halfway through I could not remember the formula, and I saw Kiran's paper on the next bench, and I looked. Once, then twice. Nobody saw. The invigilator was at the window. I got the answer and moved on. I should feel relieved. Instead my stomach has been twisted since eleven this morning. All evening I kept hearing Papa: "A low mark is fine. A false mark is not." Nobody will ever know, and that is exactly what bothers me. It is my paper and it isn't true.
Tomorrow I will tell Ma'am and ask if I can retake it, even if my marks drop. I am scared, but I would rather be scared than carry this.
Madhav

qa.q: Whose paper did Madhav look at during the test?
qa.a: Madhav looked at Kiran's paper on the next bench.

qa.q: What is Madhav feeling in the evening, and what does it suggest?
qa.a: Madhav feels guilty, with a twisted stomach even though nobody saw, which suggests the discomfort comes from Madhav's own values.

qa.q: What does Madhav decide to do the next day, and why does it matter?
qa.a: Madhav decides to tell the teacher and ask to retake the test even if the marks drop, choosing honesty over the comfort of not being caught.

qa.q: How might Papa react to Madhav's plan to tell the teacher?
qa.a: Papa would probably respect it, since Madhav remembers Papa saying a low mark is fine but a false mark is not.

grounding: A teenager feels bad after cheating even though no one saw, because it clashes with personal values.

Aparna: you awake?
Afreen: yes what's up
Aparna: I opened another tab during the online quiz. Only two questions. Full marks now
Afreen: Did the teacher notice?
Aparna: No. Nobody could. That's the strange part 😔
Afreen: Then why the sad face
Aparna: Because I know. Last week I said cheating is pointless and I meant it
Afreen: Sounds like your own rule is pinching you
Aparna: Maybe. I feel awful and I still have the mark
Afreen: What would make it feel less awful?
Aparna: Redoing those two questions in front of the teacher. I'll message before class tomorrow
Afreen: That takes guts 🙂

qa.q: How many questions did Aparna look up in the other tab?
qa.a: Aparna looked up only two questions.

qa.q: Why does Aparna feel awful even though nobody noticed?
qa.a: Aparna feels guilty because the act clashes with what Aparna said last week and believes about cheating, so the discomfort comes from inside.

qa.q: What plan does Aparna make to deal with the guilt?
qa.a: Aparna plans to message the teacher before class and redo those two questions, so the mark matches the real work.

qa.q: Why might Afreen ask what would make it feel less awful instead of saying it is fine?
qa.a: Afreen may want Aparna to find a fix that fits Aparna's own values and treats the guilty feeling as useful, not as something to brush away.

grounding: A teenager feels guilty after cheating though nobody saw, because it clashes with their own values.
